items.headline: DOJ Inquires About Nvidia’s Hugging Face Deal, Reuters Says
items.excerpt: The US Justice Department is making inquiries about Nvidia Corp.’s agreement to acquire AI model company Hugging Face for about $13 billion, part of broader regulatory scrutiny of the chip giant, Reuters reported.

items.headline: Clarity Act A 'Bipartisan Issue': Calvert
items.excerpt: Kara Calvert, vice president of US policy at Coinbase, joins Scarlet Fu and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the failure of the Clarity Act and the potential of new crypto bill after the upcoming US midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: In Position To Continue Playing Offense: Garlinghouse
items.excerpt: Brad Garlinghouse, CEO of Ripple, joins Scarlet Fu and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Crypto." Ripple said it has received final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, the latest step in its push into traditional finance. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Oracle Jumps After Projecting Return to Positive Cash Flow
items.excerpt: Oracle Corp. shares jumped after the company gave a long-term outlook for free cash flow that eased investor nerves about the potential payoff from its artificial intelligence spending.

items.headline: AI Boom Complicates Fed’s Demand Versus Supply Call, Clarida Says
items.excerpt: Former Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Richard Clarida says the Fed is weighing whether AI-driven growth represents a demand shock, which could call for higher rates, or whether productivity gains will eventually boost supply and ease inflation. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance: The Fed Decides."

items.headline: Apple Unveils Touch-Screen MacBook Pro, Reversing Long-Held Jobs Stance
items.excerpt: After two decades of spurning the idea, Apple Inc. unveiled an overhauled MacBook Pro that includes a touch screen, giving its flagship laptop a feature that has become a must-have in the personal computer industry.

items.headline: Microsoft and Alphabet Earnings Put Focus on AI Cash Flow Drain
items.excerpt: Microsoft Corp. and Alphabet Inc. shares have gone separate ways since the companies’ last earnings reports as Wall Street increasingly digs in on the way heavy artificial intelligence spending is weighing on corporate bottom lines.

items.headline: Palantir’s Defense Chief Sees Chinese Threat to Taiwan Over AI
items.excerpt: Palantir Technologies Inc.’s head of defense Mike Gallagher is warning that advances in artificial intelligence capabilities have made it more compelling for Chinese leader Xi Jinping to seize control of Taiwan, a chipmaking hub that has helped fuel the global AI boom.
